newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumer stocks rise after Socialist win.
newsitem.headline: French consumer stocks rise after Socialist win.

text.p: Investors were seeking out French consumer stocks and those with strong international exposure while dumping defence and banking companies in the wake of Sunday's election win by the Socialists, traders and analysts said.
"It is pretty clear that people are looking for blue chips or consumer stocks, while privatisation shares, particularly in the defence sector and financials are heavily penalised," said a trader.

Among the strongest risers at 1210 GMT, Eridania Beghin-Say was up 4.83 percent to 847 francs, Bic rose 3.18 percent to 877, Carrefour gained 3.17 percent to 3,910, and Galeries Lafayette added 5.71 percent to 2,220.
The Socialist party pledged during the election campaign to focus economic policy on growth, employment and a gradual increase in purchasing power.
It also said it wanted to cut value added sales tax (VAT), create 700,000 jobs for the young, and re-establish the administrative approvals process for job losses.

A big loser on the bourse was the defence sector, which was due to see the Thomson-CSF privatisation under the former government of Alain Juppe but which is looking unlikely under the new administration.

Thomson-CSF was down seven percent at 153 francs, Dassault Aviation fell 9.6 percent at 981 after being suspended limit-down twice, Dassault Electronique dropped 4.04 percent to 546 and Lagardere shed 6.95 percent to 158.

These stocks had risen strongly since the beginning of the year on the prospects of the government's sale of its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF and the pending merger between Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale.
Lagardere was a bidder for Thomson-CSF, rivalling Alcatel Alsthom.

"It is unlikely that the privatisation programme will go ahead," said an analyst at a non-domestic brokerage. "France Telecom should be privatised but the others will be slowed down or perhaps cancelled," he added.
The banking sector, which had started to consolidate with the privatisation of Credit Lyonnais and Gan, was also hit.

Sociate Generale fell 5.77 percent to 604 francs, Credit Lyonnais dropped 4.26 percent to 206.80, BNP shed 4.9 percent to 225.3 and Paribas fell 4.2 356.1. Gan, which was supposed to sell its CIC banking subsidiary before being sold off itself, was down 4.87 percent to 123.
"One of the themes which benefited the banking sector was the restructuring story, which will be delayed by the Socialist victory," an analyst said.
